label: early original-phase step (t=2-4) after a prefix of p/2/h/r/u/o/k/m
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase, at steps t=2-5 (t=2-4 holds about 97% of the activation mass, peaking at t=3). It never fires at t=0-1, in the copy phase, or at <DEL> (3 activations). Within that window it depends on which tokens came first: rate is highest when the first two originals (and prev2_tok) come from {p, 2, h, r, u, o, k, m}, with p and 2 the strongest (lift about 7x for prev2 in {2,p}). The current input also matters (z, 1, 2, g, m, 3 are best), and activation is higher on first occurrences. The largest activations are at t=3 after prefixes like "p p 2", "r 2 2", "2 p 2". The selectivity looks like a distributed, combinatorial code over the first 2-3 tokens rather than a clean rule. The t=2-4 window alone gives about 0.97 mass recall but only 4% precision. Requiring the first two tokens to be in the set gives F1 about 0.38 on dev, and adding a current-token set raises precision to 0.56 but cuts recall to 0.32.
